stem: A company director died leaving a will by which her estate is to be held on trust for her son for life and after his death to be divided between all the present and past employees of her company. The son is concerned that the trust is not workable. He has a complete list of past and present employees but is unsure that all of them can be traced.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice regarding the trust?

options.en: The trust is valid because the company still exists.
The trust is valid because there are a large number of employees who can benefit from it.
The trust is valid because there is a complete record of past and present employees.
The trust is not valid because a company cannot be a beneficiary.
The trust is not valid because the class of beneficiaries is administratively unworkable.

explanation.en: The correct answer was C. This is a fixed trust and certainty of objects is determined by whether the trustees can compile a complete list of all beneficiaries. Options A, B, D and E are wrong because the reasons given do not determine the validity of the trust.

stem: A settlor recently transferred £10m to set up a trust with the following clause: ‘The trustees shall apply the net income of the fund in making at their absolute discretion payments to any of my relatives or dependants in such amounts, at such times and on such conditions as they think fit’.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice regarding the trust?

options.en: The trust is not valid due to conceptual uncertainty.
The settlor has created a fixed trust.
The validity of the trust depends on the trustees being able to draw up a complete list of all the beneficiaries.
The beneficiaries of the trust are not entitled to equal shares of the trust income.
The trustees must ensure that the beneficiaries receive payment.

explanation.en: The correct answer was D. This is a discretionary trust (Option B is wrong), and as such the trustees are under no obligation to ensure payment to all the beneficiaries (not Option E). The test to determine conceptual certainty is the individual ascertainability test, the trustees need not draw up a complete list of the beneficiaries so not Option C. Option A is wrong because the description of the class of beneficiaries is conceptually certain.

stem: A client is seeking advice on the following gift in her husband’s will: ‘£٥٠٠,٠٠٠ to my wife, and I am confident that she will make good use of the money to take good care of our children’.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice regarding the gift?

options.en: The wife holds the money on trust for the children.
The husband intended to create a trust.
The money will be returned to the husband’s estate.
The children are entitled to the money absolutely.
The wife is entitled to the money absolutely.

explanation.en: The correct answer was E. ‘I am confident’ are precatory words, which are not emphatic enough to show certainty of intention to create a trust. As there is no trust, the answer cannot be A, B or D. The wife (who is the donee) is absolutely entitled to the money so Option C is wrong.

stem: A testator’s will made the following bequest: ‘My shares in Energy plc to my cousin from which he must ensure regular payments to his mother, my aunt, to maintain a reasonable standard of living for her’.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice regarding the gift?

options.en: The gift is void for lack of certainty of subject matter.
The gift is void for lack of certainty of objects.
The cousin can take the shares absolutely.
The aunt is the beneficiary of the trust.
The cousin is the beneficiary of the trust.

explanation.en: The correct answer was D. There was intention to create a trust with the trustee (the cousin) holding for the benefit of his mother (the testator’s aunt), who is the object (Option B is wrong). The subject matter is certain: the shares (Option A is wrong). The beneficial interest (‘reasonable standard of living’) is certain as the amount can be objectively assessed by the court. The cousin is a trustee so he cannot benefit from the shares (so not Options C or E).

stem: A testator’s will contains the following clause: ‘The bulk of my residue to be divided amongst all the faithful employees and the dependants of such employees of my former company as my executors think fit’. The testator’s company ceased operating a decade ago and the executors are unsure if there are any records left of the employees.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice regarding the gift?

options.en: The gift is valid because there are a large number of beneficiaries who can benefit from it.
The gift is valid because the executors can use extrinsic evidence to identify the beneficiaries.
The gift is not valid because the company no longer exists.
The gift is not valid because the executors cannot draw up a complete list of all the beneficiaries.
The gift is not valid because the subject matter is uncertain.

explanation.en: The correct answer was E. The subject matter of the gift is uncertain due to the word ‘bulk’. There is no valid gift so the answer cannot be A or B. Options C and D are incorrect because the reasons given are not why the gift is invalid.

topicTags: Formalities for the creation of trusts
stem: A woman was granted shares in a private company in her divorce settlement and decided to hold the shares on trust for her only son. The woman announced her intention at a family gathering and later left a voicemail to the son confirming her decision.
ask: Which of the following statements best summarises the outcome of the woman’s actions?

options.en: There is no valid declaration of trust as the woman did not execute a trust deed.
There is no valid declaration of trust as the woman did not complete the share transfer forms.
There is no valid declaration of trust as there was nothing in writing confirming the woman’s statement.
There is no valid declaration of trust as the woman did not appoint a trustee.
There is a valid declaration of trust.

explanation.topic: Formalities for the creation of trusts
explanation.en: The correct answer was E. There are no formality requirements for the creation of trusts of personalty so long as the three certainties are met. This means that there is no requirement to execute a trust deed (so Option A is wrong) and there is no requirement for the trust to be evidenced in writing (so Option C is wrong). Option B is incorrect because the issue is whether the woman has validly declared the trust; the requirement for a share transfer form is a constitution requirement, which is a separate matter. Option D is incorrect because the woman made a self-declaration of trust.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 2: Formalities for the creation of trusts

topicTags: Formalities for the creation of trusts
stem: A father is the beneficiary of a trust and wishes to transfer the benefits under the trust to his infant daughter. He informed the trustees orally of his intention to create a trust of his equitable interest for his daughter, after which he ensures that all payments received from the trustees are paid into investment accounts he set up for his daughter. He reviews the investments regularly and makes changes where necessary.
ask: Which of the following statements best summarises the outcome of the father’s actions?

options.en: There is a valid trust as the father is an active trustee.
There is no valid trust as the father should have executed a trust deed.
There is no valid trust as the father should have assigned his equitable interest to the daughter in writing.
There is no valid trust as the father should have appointed a trustee.
There is no valid trust as a beneficiary cannot also be a trustee.

explanation.topic: Formalities for the creation of trusts
explanation.en: The correct answer was A. The father has created a valid sub-trust with his daughter as the beneficiary where he is an active trustee. As the father has not dropped out of the picture entirely, there is no need to comply with the formality requirements that the disposition must be in writing and signed (so Option C is wrong). The father has made a self-declaration of trust (so Option D is wrong) and there is no requirement for a trust deed (therefore Option B is wrong). Option E is incorrect because a beneficiary can be a trustee.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 2: Formalities for the creation of trusts

topicTags: Formalities for the creation of trusts
stem: A will trust contains the following provision: ‘All my investments to be held on trust for my son until he turns 25; he is to be paid the income before then’. The testator has just died and the son, who is aged 19, met with the trustees and informed them that he does not wish to take any benefit from his father’s estate. According to the will, the testator’s daughter is the residuary legatee.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the effect of the son’s actions?

options.en: The trustees continue to hold the property on trust for the son.
The trustees must pay any income to the son.
The investments belong to the daughter.
The son’s actions have no legal effect, he should have disclaimed in writing.
The son’s actions have no legal effect, he should have disclaimed by deed.

explanation.topic: Formalities for the creation of trusts
explanation.en: The correct answer was C. The son’s oral disclaimer is valid because a disclaimer is not a disposition requiring written evidence or deed (so Options D and E are wrong). The legal effect of the disclaimer is that the investments will fall into the residue and pass to the daughter (therefore Options A and B are wrong).

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 2: Formalities for the creation of trusts

topicTags: Formalities for the creation of trusts
stem: At a family dinner celebrating her son’s 18th birthday, the mother announced that, as a birthday present for the son, she intends to hold her apartment in London on trust for him. She then wrote the same on a birthday card which she signed. A month later, the mother and son had an argument and are no longer on speaking terms. The son seeks advice on his rights to the apartment.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the outcome of the mother’s actions?

options.en: There is no valid declaration of trust as the mother should have executed a trust deed.
There is no valid declaration of trust as the mother did not appoint trustees.
There is no valid declaration of trust as she should have conveyed the apartment to him by deed.
There is a valid enforceable declaration of trust.
There is a valid declaration of trust provided the son can show that he is not a volunteer.

explanation.topic: Formalities for the creation of trusts
explanation.en: The correct answer was D. The oral declaration of trust over land was followed by evidence of trust by signed writing in the card and therefore this is a valid declaration of trust. There is no requirement for a trust deed to comply with the statutory formalities (so Option A is wrong). Option B is wrong because the mother made a self-declaration of trust. Option C is incorrect because the need for a deed of conveyance is a constitution requirement, separate to the formality requirements. Option E is wrong because it is irrelevant whether the son is a volunteer or not.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 2: Formalities for the creation of trusts

topicTags: Formalities for the creation of trusts
stem: Under a settlement, trustees are holding trust assets worth £50,000 on a bare trust for a man. The man wished to transfer his benefit to his grandchildren without incurring stamp duty. He set up a trust benefitting his grandchildren with the same trustees and orally directed the trustees to hold the investments for the benefit of the second trust.
ask: Which of the following statements best summarises the outcome of the man’s actions?

options.en: The oral direction is effective to transfer the interest to the grandchildren regardless of whether the trust assets are personalty or realty.
The oral direction is effective to transfer the interest to the grandchildren provided the trust assets are pure personalty.
The oral direction is effective to transfer the interest to the grandchildren as both trusts have the same trustees.
The oral direction is not effective because the grandchildren are volunteers.
The oral direction is not effective as it should have been done in writing.

explanation.topic: Formalities for the creation of trusts
explanation.en: The correct answer was E. There is movement of a subsisting equitable interest from the bare trust to the trust benefitting the grandchildren. This requires compliance with the statutory formalities that the declaration of trust must be in writing and signed. Options A–D are wrong because they ignore the fact that the disposition was not made in writing.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 2: Formalities for the creation of trusts

stem: A man bought a house and furnished it lavishly with expensive furniture. He took his new wife to the house for the first time, telling her to close her eyes. He opened the front door and told her to open her eyes, assuring her that everything she sees belongs to her. The man later became bankrupt and the trustee in bankruptcy is claiming the furniture. The wife claims that the furniture was a gift to her.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position with regard to the furniture?

options.en: There was a valid gift of the furniture to the wife.
The man holds the furniture on trust for his wife.
The trustee in bankruptcy can claim the furniture.
The wife can claim the furniture as she has provided marriage consideration.
The wife can sue for breach of covenant and claim damages equivalent to the value of the furniture.

explanation.en: The correct answer was C. There has been no valid delivery (by deed) of the furniture to the wife (so not Option A). He did not declare a trust of the furniture with his wife as the beneficiary so Option B is wrong. There was no covenant to benefit the wife, so Options D and E are wrong.

stem: According to the terms of a settlement signed by the settlor and his trustees, the trustees are to hold property on trust for the settlor’s daughter until she turns 25. The settlement includes a covenant by the settlor to settle all the property he is due to inherit from his mother’s estate. Two months ago, his mother’s personal representatives conveyed her house to him in accordance with the terms of her will. The settlor died last week without having transferred the house to the trustees.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice to the daughter?

options.en: The daughter can claim the house by specific performance.
The daughter can claim damages equivalent to the value of the house.
The daughter can sue the trustees for damages equivalent to the value of the house.
The trustees can sue on the daughter’s behalf and claim the house by specific performance.
The daughter has no cause of action.

explanation.en: The correct answer was E. The daughter was a volunteer and not entitled to an order of specific performance (so Option A is wrong). She was not a party to the settlement and cannot sue for damages (so Options B and C are incorrect). The trustees will not be allowed to sue on her behalf (so Option D is wrong).

stem: A man declared a trust whereby his brother is to hold the man’s house on trust for the brother’s daughter. The man wrote, ‘My brother is the trustee of my house and his daughter is the beneficiary’ on a piece of paper which he signed. He gave the paper and the deeds of his house to his brother. The man died leaving his entire estate to charity.
ask: Which of the following statements provides the best advice regarding the house?

options.en: The house will pass to the charity.
The brother holds the house on trust for his daughter.
The brother can claim the house for his daughter by specific performance.
The brother is entitled to damages to the value of the house for his daughter.
The daughter can claim the house by specific performance.

explanation.en: The correct answer was A. The trust was incompletely constituted as a deed of conveyance/transfer form is required to convey land. The daughter (beneficiary) is a volunteer and has no claim to the house. As the trust has not been constituted, and the daughter is a volunteer, Options B–E are wrong.

stem: A woman met her friend for coffee. The friend admired the bracelet the woman was wearing. She took the bracelet off and fastened it on her friend’s wrist, saying, ‘It looks good on you, you should have it’. As they were leaving the coffee shop, the woman took the bracelet back, saying that her outfit is incomplete without it. She died a week later. According to her will, all her jewellery is to be given to her sister.
ask: Which one of the following statements best describes the claim to the bracelet?

options.en: The friend can sue for the value of the bracelet.
The sister will inherit the bracelet.
The bracelet belongs to the friend.
The woman holds the bracelet on trust for her friend.
The sister holds the bracelet on trust for the friend.

explanation.en: The correct answer was B. The facts suggested an attempted inter vivos gift of the bracelet to the friend, but the gift was imperfect as the woman did not part with possession of the bracelet (she took it back). Option A is wrong as the friend is a volunteer. Option C is wrong due to the imperfect delivery of the bracelet. Options D and E are wrong as there is no indication of an intention to create a trust on the part of the woman.

stem: A husband covenanted to settle after-acquired property from his father’s estate to his marriage settlement. The beneficiaries of the settlement are the married couple, their children and the couple’s two nieces. The husband later inherited some shares from his father but he and his wife died in a car accident before he could transfer the shares to the settlement. The husband and wife have no children.
ask: Which one of the following statements best explains the nieces’ claim to the shares?

options.en: The nieces can claim the shares by specific performance.
The nieces can sue for breach of covenant and claim damages to the value of the shares.
The nieces have no claim to the shares.
The nieces can compel the trustees to sue on their behalf.
The nieces can sue the trustees for damages to the value of the shares.

explanation.en: The correct answer was C. Only the parties to the marriage and their children have marriage consideration. The nieces are volunteers. They have no right to specific performance or damages (so Options A, B, D and E are incorrect).

topicTags: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
stem: A woman worked abroad and visited her grandfather twice a year. During one such visit, her grandfather informed her that he did not expect to live long enough for her next visit. He gave her the deeds to his house and told her, ‘I want you to have the house; you have your own set of keys’. The woman’s grandfather died a month later. His will left his whole estate to a local children’s charity.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the woman’s the entitlement to the house?

options.en: The house will pass to the charity.
The woman can claim the house by estoppel.
The woman can claim the house by relying on donatio mortis causa.
There was an inter vivos gift of the house to the woman.
There is a valid trust of the house benefitting the woman.

explanation.topic: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
explanation.en: The correct answer was A. There was an imperfect lifetime gift of the house to the woman but none of the exceptions are applicable to perfect the gift. It is not Option B because the elements of estoppel were not present. It is not Option C because the donor was not anticipating death from a known cause. It is not Option D because he did not convey the house to her by deed. It is not Option E because he had no intention to create a trust.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 4: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer

topicTags: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
stem: A decade ago, the testator made a will leaving her entire estate to several animal charities. Two years ago, she suffered a stroke and her nephew decided to move in with her as her caregiver. Last year, she presented him with the deeds to her house, telling him that the house is his when she dies. A month ago, they both signed a document purporting to be a deed leaving the house to the nephew. There was no other signature on the document. The testator died last week. Her will appointed her nephew as the executor.
ask: Which of the following best describes the entitlement to the house?

options.en: The nephew can claim the house as there was a deed of conveyance in his favour.
The nephew can claim the house as he is the executor of the estate.
The nephew can claim the house by donatio mortis causa as there was delivery of the title deeds to him.
The nephew can claim the house as she had done everything in her power to transfer the house to him.
The nephew can claim the house using estoppel.

explanation.topic: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
explanation.en: The correct answer was B. The document they signed is neither a deed nor a will (lacking proper formalities) so not Option A. There was an imperfect lifetime gift of the house to the nephew but her intention to make the gift continued up to her death. As he was appointed her executor, all the requirements of Strong v Bird have been met and the gift is perfected. Option E is wrong because even though the nephew may have suffered detriment in having to look after his aunt, he did so voluntarily, not because she promised him the house. There was no evidence that she was contemplating her death so Option C is wrong. She has not done everything possible to transfer the house so Option D is wrong.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 4: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer

topicTags: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
stem: A man turned 80 last month, his only surviving next of kin are his daughter and her son. The man wanted to ensure that they should have some security in the event of his passing. He gave the title deeds to his house to his daughter, saying, ‘I want you to hold my house for your son’. He then wrote, ‘This house is for my grandson’, on the back of the one of the deeds which he signed, saying, ‘There, now it is official’. The man died last week. His will, which was executed in 1980, appointed his best friend as his executor and left his entire estate to charity.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the entitlement to the house?

options.en:
The daughter holds on trust for the grandson as there was a continuing intention to benefit the grandson and the gift was perfected on

the man’s death.
Donatio mortis causa applies and the daughter holds on trust for the grandson.
The man’s personal representatives hold the house on trust for the grandson.
The grandson is not entitled to the house.
The daughter holds on trust for the grandson as the man had done everything in his power to transfer the house to her.

explanation.topic: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
explanation.en: The correct answer was D. The man had intended to create a trust of the house with his daughter as trustee holding for the benefit of her son, but the trust was incompletely constituted as he failed to vest the legal title to the house on the daughter. None of the exceptions are applicable to perfect the trust (so all the other options are wrong).

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 4: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer

topicTags: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
stem: A woman has two children: a son from a brief relationship with a man who died before they could marry, and a daughter from her marriage. When the woman turned 80, she decided to execute a will but mistakenly assumed that any gift left in the will to her son would be invalid due to his illegitimacy. The woman’s will named her son as her executor and left her whole estate to her daughter. Later that same day, she told her son that the house belongs to him. She passed the title deeds of the house to him together with a note saying, ‘The house is yours. Love, Mum’. The next day, worried that she may not have properly conveyed the house to him, she wrote a cheque for the value of the house to him. No one else knew about the cheque and on her death, the cheque was found stapled to the will.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the entitlement to the house?

options.en: The daughter inherits the whole estate including the house.
The son is entitled to the house as he is the executor of the estate.
The son is not entitled to the house but he can claim the value of the house as represented by the cheque.
The son can claim the house by relying on donatio mortis causa.
The daughter holds the house on trust for the son.

explanation.topic: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
explanation.en: The correct answer was A. There was an imperfect lifetime gift of the house to the son. Although he was appointed as the executor of his mother’s estate, the rule in Strong v Bird is inapplicable as there was no continuing intention on the mother’s part to give him the house (the cheque negated continuing intention) so Options B and C are wrong. There was no evidence that she was contemplating her death so Option D is wrong. There was no intention to create a trust so Option E is wrong.

textbookReferences.chapter: Chapter 4: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer

topicTags: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
stem: Fifteen years ago, a man and a woman started a relationship and she moved in with him. The man was the sole owner of the house in which they lived and he paid the mortgage instalments. The couple never married but had two children together. Five years ago, the man fell in love with his personal assistant and moved in with her. Before he moved out, he told the mother of his children not to worry as the house was now hers. He told her where the title deeds to the house were kept. She started paying the mortgage instalments and spent a lot of money and effort installing a new fitted kitchen. The man is now seeking to evict the woman and their children from his house.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the woman’s entitlement to the house?

options.en: The woman is not entitled to the house as there is nothing in writing to support her claim.
The woman is not entitled to the house as she has provided no consideration.
The woman is entitled to the house as the man had done everything in his power to transfer it to her.
The woman is entitled to the house by relying on donatio mortis causa.
The woman is entitled to the house by estoppel.

explanation.topic: Exceptions to the maxim that equity will not assist a volunteer
explanation.en: The correct answer was E. The man made a promise to the woman that the house was hers and in reliance on his promise, she suffered detriment (paying mortgage instalments, installing fitted kitchen) thus perfecting the gift. The promise need not be made in writing so Option A is wrong. So long as she can prove all the elements of estoppel, consideration is not required, so Option B is wrong. None of the other exceptions are applicable so Options C and D are wrong.
